title: Experiment Safeguards and Rollback Matrix (Draft)
content:
Purpose:
- Define a concise, operationally practical set of safeguards and an explicit rollback decision matrix for cross-functional rollouts (canary / A/B) across Redwood Console. This doc is intended to be a lightweight working playbook used by product, SRE, solutions, and on-call engineering during progressive deployments.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to: new model variants, tiered routing changes, inference runtime config changes (batching/quantization), and traffic-slice experiments that affect production inference.
- Not in scope: long-lived offline experiments (bench-only), infra capacity planning unrelated to immediate rollout.
- Assumes Redwood Console has the following in place: tracing hooks, token-level cost telemetry, per-route dashboard, canary traffic slicing feature, and automated feature-flag rollback API.

Quick responsibilities (who does what):
- Product PM: owns rollout hypothesis, success metrics, experiment duration, and post-mortem.
- Release Engineer: config changes, traffic routing updates, feature flag toggles, and runbook steps.
- SRE / Oncall: monitors infra metrics, agrees on thresholds, executes immediate rollback when gate conditions met.
- Solutions / Support: customer impact triage, customer comms.

Pre-launch checklist (must be green before shifting traffic):
1) Hypothesis doc published in Confluence with primary and secondary metrics (link to linked_artifacts).
2) Canary config saved in GH and staged via feature-flag; change reviewed in PR #214.
3) Smoke test runbook validated on staging (end-to-end prompts + latency checks).
4) Observability: dashboards created (latency p50/p95/p99, error rate, downstream error counts, token cost delta, quality regression signal), and alert rules pre-set.
5) Rollback playbook and owner on-call are identified (SRE + release engineer).
6) Communication channel established (Slack #rollouts + Ops paging escalation).

Canary slicing templates (examples):
- Latency-sensitive feature: start with 0.5% of traffic (fixed shard), hold 30m -> 5% -> 20% -> 100%.
- Quality-focused evaluation (A/B): 10% control / 10% treatment for 24–72h with seeded evaluation prompts, then 25/25/50 progression.
- Cost-profile testing: route 1% traffic to quantized variant for 48h only if p95 latency delta < 20ms.

Key metrics to monitor (primary/secondary):
Primary (automated gates):
- Inference error rate (500/4xx) – automated gate if +50% relative or +0.5pp absolute increase in 15m window.
- Latency p95 for route (user-facing) – automated gate if p95 increases > 40% OR > 250ms absolute increase.
- Token-unit cost delta – automated gate if per-token cost increases > 30% relative and impacts budget estimate.
- Quality regression (seeded eval set aggregate score) – hold/gate if drop > 3 points relative to baseline.

Secondary (human-evaluated):
- Semantic regressions flagged by the black-box eval samples or user reports.
- Downstream service error amplification (e.g., rate limit on third-party APIs).

Automated gate implementation notes:
- Implement gates as short Prometheus/Datadog checks with 5m and 15m windows; majority-of-signals logic (two of four primary metrics tripped -> auto rollback).
- Use conservative thresholds initially. Gate state should trigger both an automated rollback AND an incident paging to SRE.

Rollback decision matrix (operational text table):
- Scenario A: High error spike (>= 0.5pp absolute) + p95 up -> Immediate rollback (automated), page SRE, notify PM & support.
- Scenario B: Moderate latency increase (p95 +25% but <40%) with no errors -> pause ramp, revert last config change for 10% slice, escalate to runbook review.
- Scenario C: Cost delta large (>30%) but latency/quality stable -> pause ramp, notify finance/PM, consider traffic cap or alternate quantization profile.
- Scenario D: Quality regression on seeded prompts >3 pts but no infra signals -> stop ramp, run manual prompt triage (solutions + applied-ml), potential rollback if root cause not quickly addressed.

Communication and escalation plan:
- Automated message to #rollouts when gate trips (includes chart links, traces, last deploy PR).
- SRE oncall auto-paged for immediate rollback scenarios (A).
- PM and Solutions receive summary via Slack and email for moderated scenarios (B/C/D).
- Post-rollback: 1-hour hot-standup (PM, SRE, Release Eng, Solutions) to decide containment and next steps.

Runbook: immediate rollback steps (checklist):
1) Confirm alert and corroborate in console + traces.
2) Trigger feature-flag revert or route back to control model variant (automated API call).
3) Validate revert: run 5 smoke prompts and confirm latency and error signals returned to baseline.
4) If revert fails: escalate to SRE runbook for draining nodes or taking service offline and coordinate customer comms.
5) File incident ticket (JIRA OPS-1123 style) with snapshot of metrics + PR links.
6) Kick off post-mortem within 48h with hypothesis, timeline, and action items.

Post-mortem / evaluation cadence:
- Short incident write-up due 48h after rollback or after reaching steady-state.
- Full retrospective within 7 days if customer impact or major regression.
- Add failing seeded prompts to persistent regression suite and schedule a re-test.

Open questions / items for resolution (action owners assigned inline):
- Q: Should we allow automatic rollback on a single seeded-eval regression or require combined infra+quality signals? (Owner: Priya)
- Q: How do we surface per-customer experiments that may be muted in aggregate metrics? Need per-customer dashboards. (Owner: Diego)
- Q: Define cost delta threshold for premium customers vs trial accounts. (Owner: Finance/Product)

Unresolved engineering tasks (short list):
- Hook seeded-eval pipeline into Console dashboards for live comparison (PR required — see GH PR link).
- Add a lightweight ‘rollforward’ button in Console to test fixes on a small shard without full ramp (Release Eng).

Action items (immediate):
- Ethan: implement 15m and 5m automated gates for p95 and error rate by 2025-12-05.
- Diego: prototype per-customer metric slice by 2025-12-12.
- Priya: finalize canary progression policy and publish hypothesis doc by 2025-12-01.

Notes to self / rough ideas (informal):
- Consider an internal badge for experiments that have a seeded-eval backing set (makes triage faster).
- Long-term: integrate a cost-vs-quality tradeoff visual in the rollout UI so PMs can see unit economics in the ramp slider.

References and links: see linked_artifacts list above; also Slack thread #rollouts-2025-11 for the recent discussion.

Status: draft — looking for feedback from SRE and Release Eng before we mark as in_review.

---

- 2025-11-21: added automated gate thresholds after SRE sync.
